correctness.rationale: Connected trees of diameter<=3 are exhausted by stars and double stars. For D_(a,b), all three maximal independent sets and exact random-greedy probabilities are p_u=(n−1)/(n(a+1)), p_v=(n−1)/(n(b+1)), p_0=1−p_u−p_v; independent exhaustive permutation counts matched cases including D_(2,2) and D_(2,3). The three-coordinate TV bias is max_i|p_i−1/3|. Convexity/reciprocal comparison reduces a>=2 to a=2; exact difference against a=1 is (n²−8n+9)/(3n(n−3)(n−2)), negative at n6, positive at integer n>=7. Stars have bias (n−2)/(2n), strictly worse at n>=4. Boundary orders n3,4,5,6 give unique minimizers P3,D11,D12,D22 with biases 1/6,1/12,1/15,1/9; n>=7 unique D_(1,n−3) and bias 1/3−(n−1)/(n(n−2)). Independent rational fixed-order checks n=3..100 confirm examples only; displayed algebra proves all n.

value.rationale: The smallest nontrivial diameter class with a positive uniform greedy-selection bias is a natural structural boundary given the known diameter-four family with bias tending to zero. An exact sharp value at every order, globally 1/15 at a uniquely characterized five-vertex fork, and the exceptional order-six minimizer constitute a complete, motivated optimization rather than an arbitrary small graph census.

final_claim: For all n>=3 connected trees of diameter<=3, greedy-MIS law has sharp unique fixed-n TV minimizer: P3, D11, D12, D22 for n=3,4,5,6; thereafter D_(1,n-3); global positive gap inf=1/15 uniquely at D12.
limitations: Theorem is only for trees of diameter<=3, not all n-vertex trees; known mixed-spider D_(1,b) probabilities are not new.
Finite checks do not establish the universal infinite n inequality.
